positions.name: MercadoLibre, Inc.
positions.catalyst: Brazil first-round election surprise (Sun Oct 4): Flavio Bolsonaro took ~47% vs Lula ~45%, beating polls that had Lula first. Markets read it as a pro-fiscal-discipline, business-friendly shift; Brazil ADRs gapping hard pre-market (EWZ +12.9%, ITUB +12.5%, BBD +13%, NU +10.5%, XP +16%, PAGS/STNE +15%).
positions.driver: Brazil is MELI's largest market (e-commerce + Mercado Pago fintech/credit), yet MELI is only +5.6% pre-market vs +10-16% for pure-Brazil names — a liquid, large-cap laggard with catch-up room and under the 8% no-chase line. Stock had sold off ~19% from the late-Aug high ($2,066) to $1,668 last week, so the macro catalyst lands on an oversold base. Election-surprise rallies in Brazil assets have historically carried past day one.
positions.risks: Gap-and-fade risk on a macro-driven open; runoff (late Oct) keeps political uncertainty alive; MELI has Argentina/Mexico exposure that dilutes the Brazil beta; US futures slightly red (SPY -0.2%) on higher yields; MELI downtrend since August. Hard stop $1,686.36 (-6%), just below Friday's $1,696.56 close (full gap fill = thesis broken).
